        <h2>Recent News in General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology (gr-qc)</h2>
    
            <div>
                <h3>A universal sector of $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ spectra</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Ritabrata Bhattacharya, Abhay Katyal, Oscar Varela</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We determine a universal sector of the spectrum of light operators in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ superconformal field theories arising from M5-branes wrapped on a compact hyperbolic Riemann surface $Σ_2$. We work at large $N$, analysing Kaluza--Klein fluctuations about the dual Bah--Beem--Bobev--Wecht anti-de Sitter backgrounds for general values of the twist parameter $z$. To obtain these spectra, we specialise recently derived mass operators to modes that are constant on $Σ_2$ by imposing a suitable $z$-dependent generalised $G$-structure. We then organise the resulting eigenstates into long and protected $\mathcal{N}=1$ supermultiplets with definite flavour quantum numbers. As $z$ varies, rich patterns emerge in the spectrum, including both isolated multiplets and infinite towers of multiplets, which we characterise analytically.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13938v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13938v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>$q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar, Krishan Saraswat</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Oliver H. E. Philcox</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.CO</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $σ_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>An exact rotating black hole solution in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>A. A. Araújo Filho</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We construct an exact stationary axisymmetric vacuum configuration in metric affine Kalb-Ramond gravity with zero cosmological constant. Independent variation of the metric, connection, and antisymmetric field yields the complete field equations and the algebraic relation between the physical and auxiliary geometries. A Kerr auxiliary metric and a closed corotating vacuum two form of fixed positive norm determine the physical metric. The tensor kernel contains the horizon generator, and the metrics, independent connection, and vacuum field share a smooth extension across the nonextremal physical Killing horizon and the rotation axes at finite radius for unequal deformation factors. We obtain an explicit sufficient domain for a causal exterior and an asymptotically locally flat end at fixed nonpolar angles. The physical Hamiltonian yields the timelike and null equations, equatorial effective potentials, circular orbit properties, radial stability, and perihelion advance. Numerical photon evolution determines the critical curve on an orthonormal observer screen. Its size, shape, and centroid depend on $ε=ξ_2b^2/[2(1+ξ_1b^2)]$ at fixed normalized mass scale and spin, with Kerr recovered at $ε=0$. Geometric observations probe this combination and retain an exact degeneracy between the curvature couplings. A static equatorial comparison with Mercury gives a conditional sensitivity of $2.30\times10^{-11}$ for $|2ε|$ under the stated angular convention and mass setting.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Internal translation gauging and local gravitational energy in Weyl gauge theory</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Michael Hobson, Will Barker, Anthony Lasenby</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate the local gravitational source and charges obtained by introducing translations as an internal Stückelberg redundancy in Weyl gauge theory. The internal-$T(4)$-invariant dressed coframe identifies the source of the translational potential with the existing coframe variational derivative, without introducing new dynamics. We derive an excitation/source equation and balance law whose structure is independent of the constitutive parameters of the parity-even quadratic torsion family. The gravitational self-current, defined relative to a specified gravitational/matter split and boundary representative, gives a density invariant under the internal gauge factors once its frame index is contracted with the coframe; this invariance neither establishes ordinary conservation nor identifies the density with the external translation Noether current. A surface charge follows by contraction with a covariantly constant internal direction, and we separately derive the three-sector Noether superpotential of generalized reducibility, with the asymptotic conditions for conservation of its flux. At the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR) the excitation reduces to the teleparallel superpotential and the covariant coframe--connection pair gives the Schwarzschild ADM energy; flat cosmology and transverse-traceless waves give further checks. Away from TEGR, an exact solution of New General Relativity gives a charge whose fractional difference from the Kepler mass is half the deviation of the post-Newtonian spatial-curvature parameter from unity, at the adopted normalisation; independent Hamiltonian charge matching remains open. Finally, the integrable Hamiltonian charge is invariant under covariant Lagrangian boundary terms at fixed reference normalisation and presymplectic representative.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>Bessel-Hagen currents, reducibility charges, and local gravitational energy</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Michael Hobson, Will Barker, Anthony Lasenby</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We consider whether the translation Noether current of a linearised metric spin-2 theory admits a strictly gauge-invariant local representative. For Fierz-Pauli and dynamically regular pure curvature-squared theories in four dimensions, we show that no such representative exists under the stated locality, polynomiality and covariance assumptions. A direct enumeration first excludes nonzero symmetric rank-two tensors at the dimension and derivative order of the quadratic action: in the curvature-squared case, the parity-even conservation kernel consists of the identically vanishing Lanczos--Lovelock combination, while both parity-odd coefficients vanish. Homogeneity of the actions in total derivative number then allows projection by field degree and derivative number, extending the exclusion to all finite-order local polynomial representatives with constant coefficients and no explicit coordinate dependence. The translation current nevertheless defines a nonzero conserved-current class. Independently, a constant translation is a Killing reducibility parameter of the linearised gauge symmetry and determines a nonzero linear surface-charge class, which is distinct from the quadratic energy current. A separate calculation shows why a direct compensator cancellation available in Maxwell theory fails for the metric spin-2 field, although this calculation is not needed for the current-class result. Maxwell theory, propagating free $p$-forms and Yang--Mills theory linearised about the trivial vacuum provide comparisons in which translations are not reducibility parameters and strictly gauge-invariant stress tensors exist. Gauss--Bonnet and pure flat-space $R^2$ gravity lie outside the regular scope of the result, through variational triviality and dynamical degeneracy, respectively.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Relativistic dynamical friction in Kerr-Schild coordinates</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Zipeng Wang, Francesca Chadha-Day, Katy Clough, James Maxwell</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Simulations of the evolution of matter on static metric backgrounds allow us to estimate backreaction effects like dynamical friction at first order in the matter density. Previous simulations of dynamical friction have used boosted isotropic and quasi-isotropic Kerr coordinates, which simplifies the extraction of the relevant diagnostics but results in a more complicated implementation of the evolution. In particular, the lack of horizon penetrating coordinates means that high resolutions are needed to ensure convergence, and the boosted, spinning black hole metric cannot easily be written in a closed form, making it more costly to evaluate. In this paper we describe how to reformulate the calculation of the diagnostics in the boosted Kerr-Schild frame for the non-spinning case. We verify that our implementation reproduces previous results quantifying dynamical friction in wave-like dark matter in the appropriate regimes. We discuss the subtleties of transforming diagnostic observables between frames in a 3+1 evolution and develop a general framework for this process.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13684v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13684v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

            </div>

                <h3>The Gregory-Laflamme Instability of five-dimensional Black Strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Pau Figueras, Áron D. Kovács, Shunhui Yao</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We complement and extend our recent study of the non-linear evolution of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five spacetime dimensions. First, we study time-dependent perturbations of uniform black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory and determine the growth rates as a function of the coupling. We find that for positive Gauss-Bonnet couplings, the black strings are more unstable than in general relativity in the sense that the growth rates are larger and shorter wavelengths are unstable. In the second part of the paper we show that the hyperbolicity of the equation of motion of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory is determined by an effective metric when the dynamics is restricted to spherical symmetry in the asymptotically flat directions. When the effective field theory becomes strongly coupled, as it happens near the endpoint of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of the black string, this effective metric becomes degenerate and the Cauchy evolution breaks down. Applying this criterion to uniform black strings, we find that for any positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling there is an open set of regular solutions (including the one of minimal thickness) on which the effective metric degenerates in a neighbourhood of the horizon. Therefore, we argue that these solutions cannot be attained from weakly coupled initial data by Cauchy evolution and the solutions of the linearized equations around them cannot be interpreted as approximations to nearby non-linear evolutions. We provide further evidence for this picture with non-linear simulations of the Gregory-Laflamme instability. The non-linear simulations terminate through a loss of hyperbolicity of the Tricomi or Keldysh type, depending on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Robustness of exact $SU(N)$ Einstein-Skyrme solutions: black holes, wormholes and cosmologies</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Carla Henríquez-Baez, Perla Medina, Pablo Rodríguez, Aldo Vera</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The $SU(2)$ Skyrme model admits exact solutions when coupled to General Relativity in four spacetime dimensions. Here, we demonstrate that relevant gravitational configurations, such as black holes, wormholes, and cosmologies, are robust under the extension to $SU(N)$ with an arbitrary number of flavors. We show that key physical features, such as the thermodynamic properties, the baryon number of the configurations, and the geometry, are crucially determined by the number of flavors as well as the coupling constants of the theory. In particular: first, we prove that an increase in the matter content favors the local thermal stability of spherically symmetric black holes. Second, for cosmological solutions, we demonstrate analytically that as the hadronic matter content increases, the scale factor grows more slowly due to enhanced gravitational attraction, while the expansion rate (measured by the Hubble parameter) increases as a consequence of the higher energy density. Third, we find that the throat of traversable wormhole solutions can be enlarged by increasing the number of flavors, since the energy density required to keep the throat open does not grow indefinitely but rather saturates at a finite value.</p>
                </div>
                <div>

            <div>
                <h3>On the Utility of Textbooks in Understanding the Renaissance of General Relativity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Bernadette Lessel</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: physics.hist-ph</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>This paper argues for the historical utility of general relativity textbooks written during, or shortly before, the Renaissance of general relativity. More so than research papers, textbooks offer a narrative account of the field--one that may differ substantially from the accounts of other authors addressing the same subject. Textbooks on general relativity therefore constitute a distinctive form of testimony to the intellectual forces that shaped general relativity, particularly during its reinvention period from 1955 to the mid-1970s. A second pillar of this argument is the observation that nearly all principal investigators at the research centers previously identified by Lalli et al.--centers that functioned as intellectual epicenters of the Renaissance of general relativity--eventually produced a textbook associated with their own school of thought. To situate this observation within the broader development of the field, the paper presents a concise history of general relativity textbooks from the theory's inception in 1915-16 to the 1980s. This history illustrates one way in which textbooks can serve as sources for reconstructing the intellectual dynamics of the Renaissance of general relativity.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Jasper Nongmaithem, Deepak Kumar Kar, Ayush Kumar, Shreeya Rajesh Parab, David Dudal, Subhash Mahapatra</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>The School on Gravity: from motion to commotion</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Vitor Cardoso, Jose María Ezquiaga, Julio Parra-Martinez, Laura Sberna, Gustavo J. Turiaci, Lieke van Son</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Understanding the gravitational interaction is one of the great scientific endeavors of the 21st century. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of gravitational waves in 2015, and subsequent detections by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration, have marked a revolutionary step forward in physics and astrophysics by opening an entirely new window for exploring the Universe. Future upgrades to these detectors, along with upcoming facilities such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and radio and optical instruments, promise other breakthrough discoveries that the next generation of scientists will need to interpret. The School on Gravity (22--26 June 2026, Copenhagen) aimed to introduce junior scientists--graduate students and advanced undergraduates with a background in general relativity--to a wide range of foundational topics in the exciting new field of gravitational-wave physics. Topics spanned from the theory of motion, to new challenges introduced by quantum physics, to the astrophysics of black holes and source modeling for gravitational-wave detectors. The School on Gravity took place at the legendary Auditorium A of the Niels Bohr Institute, inviting students and lecturers to challenge current paradigms in gravitational physics in the spirit of the quantum revolution that unfolded in this very room. These lecture notes aim at opening up those new ideas presented in Auditorium A to the rest of the scientific community.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Compactly supported instability of Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metrics</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Erwann Delay</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: math.DG</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>On the Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metric of dimension $n\geq 4$, we show that the destabilizing TT tensor of Ozuch lies in the image of the ``TT-tensor machine''. By continuity, it can then be approximated, in suitable weighted Sobolev spaces, by smooth compactly supported TT tensors, on which the stability quadratic form is still negative. This proves instability in the usual sense for noncompact manifolds. To our knowledge, no exact smooth compactly supported destabilizing TT tensor was known before, even in 4D.</p>

            <div>
                <h3>Integrable auxiliary field sigma model and the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Nicola Baglioni, Daniele Bielli, Parita Shah, Gabriele Tartaglino-Mazzucchelli</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We describe a family of two-dimensional metric deformations that preserve integrability. The seeds are (classically) conformal integrable field theories and the deformations are directly related to different classes of auxiliary field sigma models. We introduce a master action connecting deformations by Lie-algebra-valued auxiliary fields, the so-called $ν$-frame, to deformations by two Lorentz-charged scalars. These auxiliary scalar fields can be identified as Beltrami differentials of an auxiliary two-dimensional metric, providing a direct connection with the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations. For Weyl-invariant seed matter theories, the auxiliary metric sector is described by a reduced gravitational potential. We show that the resulting framework preserves classical Lax integrability whenever the seed matter theory admits a Lax representation of its equations of motion on a generic curved two-dimensional spacetime. Finally, within the Lorentz-invariant family and the zweibein deformations of conformal matter theories considered here, we identify $T\bar{T}$ as the only deformation that can be interpreted as a field-dependent coordinate transformation.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>Flip-Flop Shocks and Tori in Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton Accretion onto Rotating Kerr-Weyl Black Holes and Their Quasi-Periodic Variability</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Orhan Donmez, Imtiaz Khan, G. Mustafa</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.HE</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We present GRHD simulations of Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion onto a rotating black hole in Weyl conformal gravity, described by the Kerr-Weyl metric. The equatorial flow is evolved for spins a=0.9M and a=0.5M and several Weyl coefficients, which enter through an effective curvature parameter k, and is compared with Kerr runs sharing the same setup. For the k considered, the horizon, ISCO and test-particle frequencies differ from Kerr by at most ~2%. However, the curvature term grows as kr^2 and acts at the accretion radius R_acc. The flow is controlled by one quantity, eta=|k|R_acc^3/M, the ratio of curvature-induced to Newtonian acceleration at R_acc. For eta<~0.03 a stable shock cone forms, indistinguishable from Kerr. For eta~0.2-0.3 the anti-de Sitter-like term traps shocked gas behind the black hole and drives persistent flip-flop oscillations. For eta>~1.6 the cone is destroyed and an oscillating torus forms. Spin modifies only the inner few gravitational radii and does not change the regime. In strongly deviating models the mean accretion rate is 1.7-3 times the Kerr value and varies by 20-60% rms, versus 0.1-1% in Kerr-like flows. The power spectra show global QPOs with fundamentals at 2.9-4.8 Hz for a 10 Msun black hole, with harmonic ladders whose 3:2 and 2:1 ratios come from one non-sinusoidal oscillation, not resonances. These lie in the low-frequency QPO band and are unrelated to test-particle frequencies (~70-200 Hz). They scale as f_0=xi f_K(R_acc), with xi~0.7-1.1 for stable cones and xi~0.23-0.38 for flip-flop and torus regimes. Strong oscillations would be detectable within seconds for a bright Galactic source. The required |k| exceeds galactic-rotation-curve values by 18-36 orders of magnitude, so a detected shock-driven QPO would measure a local deviation from Kerr, and its absence would constrain |k|.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>On the quantum statistical relation and the covariant phase space Hamiltonian</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>José Luis V. Cerdeira, Tomás Ortín</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We show how the covariant phase space Hamiltonian can be constructed in theories in which some of the fields have gauge freedoms. The addition to the action of boundary terms that guarantee the well-posedness of a variational principle and its exact gauge invariance for the prescribed boundary conditions turn out to be essential in this construction. The same ingredients are essential in the use of the action in the framework of Gibbons and Hawking's Euclidean approach to Quantum Gravity and we show how the on-shell action constructed with a Lagrangian with those properties can be expressed in terms of the covariant phase space Hamiltonian. We compute the Hamiltonian of several theories, one of which has Chern--Simons terms, using our prescription and show that, in black-hole backgrounds, the Hamiltonian gives directly the quantum statistical relation including terms related to non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.</p>

                <h3>General relativity and its modifications as effective field theories of $GL(4)$ breaking</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Tommaso Viacava, Omar Zanusso</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>

            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>

                <div>
                    <p>We discuss General Relativity and some of its modifications as effective field theories of the breaking of the affine general linear group using the coset approach and the Maurer-Cartan form. While the ultimate goal is to break the symmetry down to the Lorentz subgroup, we argue that there are three interesting breaking cascades in which the affine general linear group is first broken to a larger subgroup that contains the Lorentz group. In all cases, the breaking of translations always generates Goldstone modes that can be interpreted as metric degrees of freedom. We argue that the effective field theories that emerge as a result of the different breaking patterns are all dynamically equivalent at the lowest order of the derivative expansion, e.g., using Einstein-Hilbert-like actions, but can differ beyond the leading order.</p>

                <h3>Codimension-Zero Holographic Complexity and Spectral Three-Point Correlators</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Masamichi Miyaji, Shan-Ming Ruan, Shono Shibuya, Kazuyoshi Yano</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>

                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Holographic complexity is expected to capture the linear growth of black hole interiors, with quantum corrections ultimately leading to a late-time saturation. We develop a spectral formulation of holographic complexity measures associated with codimension-zero bulk regions in the framework of the complexity=anything proposal. The corresponding generating function of complexity is governed by three-point correlation functions of the density of states, establishing a direct connection between bulk geometric observables and nonperturbative Euclidean spacetime wormholes. We find that the codimension-zero holographic complexity reduces to the sum of two codimension-one contributions and exhibits a universal time evolution, characterized by an exponentially long regime of linear growth followed by saturation at the Heisenberg time. The late-time plateau is a direct result of the spectral level repulsion, a generic feature of quantum chaotic systems, thereby providing a universal mechanism for the saturation of holographic complexity. We also develop a complementary operator interpretation, in which Euclidean wormhole corrections render the semiclassical basis of fixed-complexity states overcomplete. Constructing a complete orthonormal basis then yields well-defined holographic complexity operators that reproduce the same universal time evolution. Our results establish a unified connection among black hole interiors, chaotic spectral statistics, and Euclidean wormholes in quantum gravity.</p>

                <h3>Learning Schwarzschild Geodesic Motion with Lagrangian Neural Networks</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Sukru Caglar, Sena Kalabalik, Abdullah Umut Hamzaogullari, Arkadas Ozakin</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: cs.LG</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn dynamics from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving accelerations through the Euler--Lagrange equation, providing a variational inductive bias that improves physical consistency over purely data-driven models. LNNs have recently been extended to general relativistic settings, leaving Schwarzschild geodesics as an open challenge. Training on complex relativistic systems is hindered by the diversity of the dynamics, as well as numerical instabilities and the difficulty of adequately sampling physically relevant, diverse orbital regimes. We introduce two coordinated improvements: a decoupled position--velocity normalization scheme that independently rescales each coordinate and its time derivatives, reweighting acceleration targets to balance contributions across all channels; and an energy-constrained log-uniformly sampled dataset generation strategy informed by the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) structure. With these improvements, our model accurately reproduces perihelion precession and relativistic time dilation, conserves energy and angular momentum to within a few percent even after completing multiple orbits around the central mass and predicts orbital trajectories across eight orbital scenarios in close, medium, and far-field regimes. These results establish that LNNs, augmented with physically motivated normalization and sampling, can reliably learn geodesic dynamics in curved spacetime. Our work also represents the first successful training of LNNs on Schwarzschild geodesics and offers a promising direction for data-driven modeling of complex relativistic systems.</p>

                <h3>Binary Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Nikita M. Shirokov, Ilya Nachevsky</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We present what are, to our knowledge, the first 3D numerical-relativity evolutions of wormhole binaries: pairs of massive Ellis-Bronnikov drainholes held open by a ghost scalar field. Each throat is an unstable fixed point whose e-fold time matches the González-Guzmán-Sarbach linear rate to within 1.9%. Two throats obey a charge-sign rule: like scalar charges repel and opposite charges attract, with a measured attraction-to-repulsion ratio of $1.462\pm0.022$ against the predicted 3/2, so only opposite-signed pairs merge. A head-on collision forms a common MOTS around both still-open throats, born with about their combined area. The horizon then loses 28% of its area as it swallows the phantom field, and by $t=100$ lies within 1.4% of the Schwarzschild radius of the pair's mass, still shrinking. Fly-by pairs form no horizon and both mouths inflate, the one nearest capture radiating the most gravitational-wave energy measured. A lone collapsing throat sheds its seeded quadrupole as a burst ringing at the Schwarzschild frequency of the black hole it becomes, and every encounter radiates its own burst of gravitational waves and a scalar dipole of comparable energy and negative sign. A throat survives at most a few orbital periods for any plausible perturbation, and the negative-energy dipole would pump rather than drain the orbit, so these binaries have no inspiral.</p>

                <h3>Causality, Redshift, and Matching-Scale Cancellation for Reflective Black-Hole Horizons</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Masahiro Kaminaga</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-09</b></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The Boltzmann flux reflectivity used in quantum-horizon models does not by itself define a causal black-hole boundary response. We study two related questions for stationary Schwarzschild scattering. First, a classical Hardy-space condition excludes an exact Boltzmann modulus on the entire positive frequency axis for any nonzero bounded causal reflection amplitude at a fixed matching plane. We construct causal completions that preserve the modulus on any prescribed finite band. Second, we prove a low-frequency outer-phase expansion for a class of completions with fixed profiles and a common Boltzmann slope, including an exact-band completion and a smooth crossover completion. The logarithmic coefficient is common to this class, while the linear constant is an explicit functional of the completion. When the fixed proper-frame cutoff is redshifted to the matching surface and the local temperature is the Tolman redshift of the Hawking temperature, the outer phase cancels the leading logarithmic dependence of the propagation phase on the matching distance. The geometric remainder is quadratic in the proper distance, while a separate dispersive remainder depends on the completion. This is a low-energy comparison of specified response families, not an exact matching invariance or a phase fixed by causality alone. In an axial Schwarzschild example at a fixed matching plane, accounting for the predicted linear-delay difference reduces the maximum relative cavity-factor difference between two cutoffs from about $21\%$ to $0.11\%$ on the sampled frequency band. A passive quantum completion supplies the associated absorption-noise relation and checks the consistency of the asymptotic output.</p>

                <div>
                    <p><i>Nephtalí Eliceo Martínez Pérez, Cupatitzio Ramírez Romero</i></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Geometric Inflation adds an infinite tower of curvature invariants to the Einstein-Hilbert action while preserving certain key features such as leading to second order modified Friedmann equations for FRW backgrounds. Sourcing them with a perfect barotropic fluid can easily produce a slow-roll inflationary regime, no inflaton field is required. In this work, we perform the Wheeler-DeWitt quantization of minisuperspace Geometric Inflation models. First, we construct an effective 1D FRW action and perform the Hamiltonian formulation using both Ostrogradsky's approach and Dirac's algorithm for constrained systems. The Lagrangian and Hamiltonian treatment of the perfect fluid is based on Schutz's formalism. Second, we postulate the Wheeler-DeWitt equation and investigate its solutions both analytically and numerically. For radiation we are led to a system of fractional differential equations for which we use Caputo fractional derivative operator. We construct wave packets in momentum space, with the fluid's variable acting as external time parameter.</p>

                <div>
                    <p><i>Abdias Aires, Tatsuya Daniel</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>

            <p>Categories: hep-ph</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>We study the reheating epoch and total bounce-to-present expansion in modified loop quantum cosmology using current observational determinations of the scalar amplitude and spectral index. We consider the power-law plateau potential, whose normalization is determined independently from the observed values of the scalar amplitude and spectral index. We find that, for the kinetic-energy-dominated initial conditions, the quantum-bounce regime is remarkably insensitive to this normalization, while the subsequent inflationary and reheating evolution shows a more appreciable dependence. We then investigate the sensitivity of the results to the inflationary potential by considering the Starobinsky and polynomial chaotic potentials. The reheating e-fold number and reheating temperature are found to depend strongly on both the form of the potential and, in the polynomial case, the branch selected. In contrast, the total bounce-to-present expansion satisfies the conservative bound N > 129 over the ranges considered here and remains close to the characteristic scale found in LQC. Moreover, the difference between mLQC-I and LQC is remarkably stable for all three potentials. These results suggest that reheating is strongly model dependent, whereas the small systematic shift in the total expansion is primarily associated with the different background quantum geometries of LQC and mLQC-I.</p>

                <h3>Asymptotic AEther Misalignment and Universal-Horizon Mechanics</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Walter Arata, Moustafa Ismail, Stefano Liberati, David Mattingly, Luke Martin, Giulio Neri</i></p>

                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Universal horizons trap even arbitrarily fast signals, providing a test of black-hole thermodynamics in theories with a preferred time direction. In Einstein--aether theory, this direction is defined by a dynamical field, the aether, that can remain non-aligned relative to stationary time at infinity. In particular, for asymptotically anti-de Sitter black holes, it was so far impossible to recover a first law of black-hole mechanics when such asymptotic tilt of the aether is present. Here, we resolve this issue for an exact family of static, spherically symmetric solutions. Using the covariant phase-space formalism, we identify the asymptotic tilt and the decaying part of the aether field as a boundary source and its conjugate response. Allowing both to vary independently obstructs the definition of an energy that generates time translations. Fixing either quantity, or imposing a relation between them, restores such an energy, while externally varying the boundary data introduces work into the first law. The energies obtained by fixing the source or its response are related by a Legendre transformation. At the universal horizon, heat includes both the metric area contribution and an irreducible aether energy flux. The resulting balance separates work at infinity from horizon heat and explains why the physical temperature cannot generally be inferred from the coefficient of an area variation in the black-hole mass.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>We report the first Monte Carlo simulation of quantum field theory on Euclidean de Sitter space, $S^4$. Rather than discretizing space, we use a spectral lattice based on spherical harmonics, keeping all symmetries exact at finite cutoff. For a massless $λφ^4$ theory, the zero-mode distribution reproduces the Starobinsky-Yokoyama equilibrium at weak coupling, and deviations closely follow the one-loop renormalization of $λ$. At strong bare coupling, the renormalized quartic coupling saturates near the ceiling of the one-loop renormalization-group flow. This saturation is the de Sitter counterpart of the triviality mechanism that bounds the Higgs mass in flat space. Our results confirm nonperturbatively that the infrared divergences of light scalars in de Sitter are correctly resummed by the stochastic formalism. More broadly, this work opens up de Sitter space to lattice Monte Carlo methods.</p>

Using the four-loop $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ beta function continued to $D=4+2ε$, we determine the largest dimension $D_{\mathrm{pt}}=4+2ε_{\mathrm{pt}}$ below which successive loop corrections to the fixed point remain hierarchically ordered under a specified ratio criterion, and map $D_{\mathrm{pt}}$ over color and flavor numbers for fermions in the fundamental representation of $SU(N)$. At $D=5$, we construct rational anomalous dimensions with a fixed, pole-regularized denominator inspired by the functional renormalization group (fRG). Matching to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ series through one, two, and three loops produces progressively smaller shifts in the critical flavor number and coupling at the ultraviolet--infrared merger (the point where the infrared and ultraviolet fixed points coincide), yielding $N_f^{\mathrm{cr}}\simeq 2.09 \, N$ at large $N$ in the three-loop construction. This low-order stabilization, together with qualitative evidence from fRG flows including higher gauge operators, suggests a potential merger scenario that bounds the candidate asymptotically safe region in flavor number. The resulting color--flavor map provides guidance for five-dimensional model building by displaying both the baseline perturbative-control boundary and the candidate three-loop merger boundary. Four-loop matching, however, retains an interacting ultraviolet fixed point beyond the three-loop merger boundary, with no merger found for integer $2\le N\le15$ and $0\le N_f/N\le11/2$. The sensitivity of the fixed-point structure to higher-order terms leaves both scenarios open, highlighting fixed-point annihilation as a potential constraint on five-dimensional asymptotic safety.</p>

                <h3>Evidence for orbital eccentricity supports a hierarchical origin for GW231123</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Baoxiang Wang, Tao Yang, Zhoujian Cao, Bin Hu, Xikai Shan, Rong-Gen Cai</i></p>

                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.HE</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>GW231123 is the most massive binary black hole merger observed to date and one of the most intriguing hierarchical merger candidates in the pair-instability mass gap. Its exceptionally large inferred component spins and remarkably short in-band duration make the source highly sensitive to waveform physics near merger. Here we show that GW231123 is better described as an eccentric binary black-hole merger. We analyse data over 11--448 Hz using the eccentric, spin-precessing effective-one-body waveform model TEOBResumS--Dalí, accounting for detector calibration uncertainty. We measure $e_{5.5\,\mathrm{Hz}}=0.34^{+0.12}_{-0.23}$ at 90\% credibility and obtain a Bayes factor of 10.2 in favour of the eccentric model over its quasi-circular counterpart. GW231123-like injection--recovery studies further show that analyses starting at 20 Hz, as in previous studies, can obscure this eccentricity. Including eccentricity substantially changes the spin inference, weakening the preference for a near-extremal secondary spin and lowering its posterior median to $a_2\simeq0.7$, close to the characteristic spin expected for a black-hole merger remnant. These results provide a coherent dynamical interpretation of GW231123, in which residual eccentricity, a mass-gap black hole, and a remnant-like spin arise naturally from a hierarchical merger channel in a dense environment.</p>

                <div>
                    <p><i>Fang-Stars Wei, Zelin Zhang, Zhenyu Zhang, Bin Chen</i></p>

            <p>Categories: astro-ph.HE</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Autocorrelation in black hole movies encodes the time delays and angular separations between gravitationally lensed images, offering a means of testing the spacetime geometry. Using an orbiting hot spot in the parametrized Johannsen-Psaltis metric with a single deformation parameter, we investigate the ability of lensing-induced correlations to distinguish departures from Kerr. From ray-traced movies, we extract the slope (k) and intercept (b) of an approximately linear secondary ridge in the time-angle autocorrelation map as potential future observables. Variations in the spin and the metric deformation parameter produce distinctive trajectories in the (k,b) plane, allowing the two observables to jointly constrain both parameters when the orbital radius, observer inclination, and orbital angular velocity are specified. By varying the orbital angular velocity, we construct a Kerr reference region in the (k,b) plane, and we find that, for some low-spin configurations with negative deformation parameters, the measured slope-intercept pairs of the secondary peaks lie outside this reference region. This feature appears for sub-Keplerian, Keplerian, and super-Keplerian motion, indicating that secondary-ridge measurements from black hole flare movies have the potential to distinguish non-Kerr signatures.</p>

                <h3>The variance of the CMB temperature gradient: a dependence on the spatial orientation and anisotropy of a multiply connected Universe</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Ralf Aurich, Martin J France, Frank Steiner</i></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>

                <div>
                    <p>In the present work we develop a model--independent method to reveal the underlying patterns of anisotropy and geometry in CMB temperature maps. This method, based on the rho-statistics and a process of mask--sweeping, unveils faint but persistent geometrical and periodic structures characterising the anisotropy of the CMB in a universe with 3-torus topology. We assess that the patterns detected over large ensembles of toroidal maps match geometrically to the layouts of expected circles-in-the-sky. The mask--sweeping method explores the whole CMB over 768 mask orientations. Thus we are able to re-verify the linear relation between L the size of the cubic torus and rho the standard deviation of the normalised variance of the CMB temperature gradient. This confers a finite size s of approximately 3 Hubble lengths to our Universe with toroidal topology. Furthermore, it is shown that the violation of statistical isotropy is so faint that this has almost no influence on the linear relation between rho and L. A topology like the cubic toroidal one imposes to our Universe periodic conditions (that can be seen as periodic boundary conditions) which constrain the global degree of inhomogeneity and a zero average curvature. We demonstrate here that rho is not only a statistical signature of the spatial finiteness and size of our Universe (may its topology be simply or multiply connected) but also outlines the patterns of anisotropy of the CMB with the help of the mask--sweeping process.</p>

                <h3>Gravitational radiation from a photon on the light ring: multipole fluxes and the logarithmic divergence</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Enrico Barausse</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>A massless particle on the circular null geodesic of a Schwarzschild or Kerr black hole radiates gravitational waves at all multipoles $\ell$ with a power that falls off only as $1/\ell$, so that the total instantaneous power is logarithmically divergent. We derive this result analytically from the Zerilli--Regge--Wheeler and Teukolsky equations with a null stress-energy tensor as source, and find that both the power radiated to infinity and the power absorbed by the horizon approach $\dot{E}_\ell\to g(a) κE^2/(M^2\ell)$, where $E$ is the energy of the particle, $M$ the mass of the black hole and $a$ its spin, with $κ=0.063653$ and a spin factor $g(a)$, for which we obtain, for any spin, the closed form $g=27M^2(r_0-M)/[r_0^2(r_0+3M)]$ in terms of the radius $r_0$ of the Kerr light ring. The $1/\ell$ behavior has two causes: the near-resonance of the photon with the quasinormal modes, which prevents any exponential suppression at large $\ell$, and a cancellation in the source that is specific to massless particles, which reduces the power per multipole by a factor $\ell^2$ with respect to a generic source. At leading order half of the radiation falls into the black hole, and we compute the first correction to this equal split in the non-spinning case. The same analysis describes massive particles on orbits close to the light ring, where the mass turns the $1/\ell$ law into an exponential cut-off. We recover the dominant, even-parity term of the geodesic synchrotron radiation formulae for massive particles of Breuer, Ruffini, Tiomno and Vishveshwara (1973), but we find that their odd-parity term is too small by a factor of four. All results are checked against numerical solutions, up to $\ell=12800$ in Schwarzschild and $\ell=800$ in Kerr.</p>

                <h3>Testing General Relativity with Binary Lens Microlensing Events</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Xinyang Jin, Shuo Cao, Xuanni Chen, Yalong Nan, Xuchen Tai, Shuxun Tian</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Einstein's General Relativity (GR), which has been precisely tested on galaxy and solar system scales, is still poorly constrained in extremely weak gravitational fields (with dimensionless Newtonian potentials of $Φ\sim 10^{-8}$). In this Letter, we propose a new method to probe such a weak-field regime of gravity and measure the spatial curvature generated per unit mass. Specifically, binary microlensing events provide a laboratory to measure the parameterized post-Newtonian (PPN) parameter ($γ$), by combining the lensing mass ($M_{\rm lens}^{\rm GR}$) inferred from microlensing with the dynamical mass ($M_{\rm dyn}$) determined from interferometric astrometry. Astrometric tracking of binary lenses was previously hindered by their faintness and minuscule angular separations (typically a few milliarcseconds). This limitation has been alleviated by the deployment of GRAVITY+, which pushes the instrument's sensitivity and astrometric precision to unprecedented heights. Based on astrometric simulations of the binary microlensing event ASASSN-22av, we directly estimate $γ$ at the precision of ~23%. Such test of GR in the extremely weak-field regime can be further improved to much higher precision (~3%), based on more binary microlensing events with precise determination of the dynamical/lens mass.</p>

                <div>
                    <p><i>Ahmad Al-Badawi, Shokhzod Jumaniyozov</i></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>

                <div>
                    <p>We investigate the dynamics of charged test particles around a Letelier black hole, i.e. a black hole surrounded by a cloud of strings (CoS), in Kalb-Ramond (KR) gravity, immersed in an external, asymptotically uniform magnetic field aligned with the symmetry axis. The geometry depends on the CoS parameter and on the Lorentz-violating KR parameter only through a single combination of the two, so that the two effects can compensate each other and the Schwarzschild metric is recovered when both parameters are equal. Because the spacetime is not Ricci flat, the Wald potential is not a solution of the Maxwell equations; we show that the regular source-free magnetic test field is given in closed form by a Gauss hypergeometric function of the radial coordinate, which reduces to the Wald solution in the Schwarzschild limit. Using this exact field we derive the equations of motion, the effective potential, the circular orbits, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), representative escaping, captured and curled trajectories, and the orbital, radial and vertical epicyclic frequencies in closed form; all frequency expressions are cross-checked against direct numerical integration of the full equations of motion. Within the relativistic precession model, we perform a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis of the twin-peak high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) of GRO J1655-40, XTE J1550-564 and GRS 1915+105 for four nested models, complemented by nested sampling to compute Bayesian evidences and to weight the two (Larmor and anti-Larmor) magnetic modes of the posterior. The Schwarzschild model is excluded for GRO J1655-40 and XTE J1550-564, with a difference in the Akaike information criterion of about 110.</p>

                <h3>Sharing of Gaussian tripartite steering in de-Sitter space</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Xin-Ze Song, Xiao-Li Huang, Shu-Min Wu</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate the redistribution and directional properties of Gaussian tripartite quantum steering in de-Sitter space within the continuous-variable framework. By expressing the Bunch-Davies vacuum in terms of the open-chart modes through a Bogoliubov transformation, we derive the covariance matrix of the resulting multipartite Gaussian state and analyze both one-to-two and two-to-one steering configurations. We find that de-Sitter curvature generally suppresses the steering initially shared among the accessible modes, but its influence depends strongly on the steering direction. In particular, while some steering configurations undergo sudden death at finite curvature, two-to-one steering toward a nongravitational mode remains finite throughout the parameter range considered, demonstrating a robustness of tripartite steering absent in its bipartite counterpart. Remarkably, the maximum steering asymmetry occurs at the critical point at which steering in one direction undergoes sudden death, marking the transition from two-way to one-way steering. We further show that the de-Sitter gravitational field can generate tripartite steering involving modes separated by the cosmological horizon. Depending on the steering partition, this curvature-induced steering exhibits persistent one-way or asymmetric two-way behavior, as well as a sudden-birth transition from one-way to two-way steering. These results demonstrate that de-Sitter curvature not only degrades preexisting quantum correlations but also redistributes and generates directional multipartite steering across causally disconnected regions.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>We develop a novel systematic method for constructing exact, static, and asymptotically flat black-hole solutions in shift-symmetric and $Z_2$-symmetric beyond Horndeski theories. In contrast to previous studies, our approach does not rely on the restrictive reciprocal condition $g_{tt}g_{rr}=-1$, allowing for more general geometries characterized by two independent metric functions. The resulting solution space contains two qualitatively distinct types of hair originating from different branches of the theory. One branch is characterized by khronometric hair, while the other by genuine scalar hair. In both, the scalar profile defines a nontrivial preferred foliation, but the shift-symmetry Noether current and the associated propagating degree of freedom are trivial for the former and nonvanishing for the latter. Focusing mainly on the second branch, we derive several distinct families of exact black-hole solutions. In general, these solutions are singular and exhibit primary scalar hair associated with an independent scalar charge. Nevertheless, we demonstrate that they can be regularized to yield regular black-hole or solitonic configurations, for which the scalar hair becomes secondary. We further investigate the stability properties of these solutions under linear perturbations by analyzing the axial sector and the monopole $(\ell=0)$ mode of the even-parity sector. For representative solutions with scalar hair, the perturbative analysis provides evidence for linear stability under the modes considered.</p>

                <h3>Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Sergey N. Solodukhin</i></p>

            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/λ$, where $λ\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/λ)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $Σ_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $Σ_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.</p>

                    <p>The Dolgov-Kawasaki instability tests the local scalaron response in metric $f(R)$ gravity, but does not determine strong-field horizon dynamics. For a nonzero massive scalaron tail transmitted to a nondegenerate Cauchy horizon, a conditional fixed-background estimate gives a nonintegrable contribution to generalized entropy focusing.                 <div>
                    <p>We study holographic dark energy models constructed from generalized entropy functionals and local infrared cut-offs. Three entropies (Barrow and the three and five-parameter generalized entropies) are each combined with the Granda-Oliveros (GO) cut-off and two extensions, one adding a $γH^{-2}$ term and one a $γ\ddot{H}/H$ term, the latter raising the dark-energy evolution equation to second order. The nine resulting models are constrained against DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ and a Planck compressed CMB likelihood through an MCMC analysis, and compared using the Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. The Hubble constant is stable across all models. The $H^{-2}$ term is unconstrained in every case, as it becomes relevant only in the far future, and never improves on the GO cut-off. The $\ddot{H}/H$ term, instead, is tightly constrained for Barrow and $S_5$, where it improves the fit substantially, but not for $S_3$. The best fit is obtained for Barrow entropy with the $\ddot{H}/H$ cut-off, yet the Barrow exponent remains compatible with zero in all cases. The data thus favour a higher-order infrared cut-off, while showing no significant evidence for a departure from the Bekenstein-Hawking area law. We also investigate the dark energy equation of state (EoS) of $S_3$ and $S_5$, discovering quintessence-like behavior and phantom crossing.</p>

                <h3>Bulk-boundary decompositions and exact perfect fluid stellar distributions</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Sudan Hansraj, Christian G. Boehmer, Ndumiso Buthelezi</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The decomposition of the Ricci scalar in terms of bulk and boundary terms gives rise to an interesting gravitational field theory as proposed by Böhmer and Jensko (BJ). BJ went on to suggest functional forms of the bulk contributions in the Lagrangian. For the purposes of astrophysical modelling the boundary terms are non-dynamical and the entire theory is built from the bulk contribution only. The field equations for a stellar perfect fluid distribution are obtained against the background of a conformostatic metric. Since the linear form of the function of the bulk term is equivalent to Einstein we probe the next level of complexity namely the pure quadratic case. The field equations are substantially more complicated than Einstein's equations. The equation of pressure isotropy proves intractable even with simple choices of one of the geometric potential functions. Accordingly we analyse the case of the potentials varying inversely with the radius. Viable models do not arise in this case and so we postulate a proportional relationship between the potentials. It turns out that a physically reasonable shell of isotropic fluid may be constructed that satisfies elementary physical requirements. Finally we investigate the isothermal fluid where both density and pressure go as the inverse square law of the radius. This results in fluid behaviour that is comparable to that in the corresponding Einstein model.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>We present a non-perturbative formulation of quantum gravity in asymptotically flat spacetimes using Witten's cubic open string field theory (OSFT) on unstable D-branes. Given that the massless spin-2 sector of the closed string spectrum inherently encodes the degrees of freedom of quantum gravity, we establish this connection by mapping on-shell closed string excitations directly to gauge-invariant operators in OSFT, realizing a concrete flat-space analogue of the AdS/CFT correspondence. By evaluating the OSFT correlation functions of these operators perturbatively around the tachyon vacuum, we systematically reproduce the all-orders genus expansion of the closed string S-matrix for the associated states. This demonstrates that closed string theory-and thus quantum gravity-emerges dynamically from the open string tachyon vacuum, establishing Witten's OSFT as a fully calculable, non-perturbative framework for flat-space quantum gravity.</p>

                <h3>Note on decoherence of the cosmological background by thermal perturbations in the language of open quantum systems</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Alexander Kulyabin</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study, within a toy model, how a thermal bath of cosmological perturbations can decohere the homogeneous degrees of freedom of the universe, treating the perturbations as an environment in the framework of open quantum systems. In contrast to several earlier approaches, instead of tracing out the perturbations from a semiclassical ansatz for the total wave function, we incorporate their cosmological backreaction through an effective second-order coupling and derive a master equation. Our toy model consists of a spatially flat semiclassical inflationary universe with a clock field in the slow-roll regime, while scalar cosmological perturbations in an assumed thermal-like state constitute the environment. One of the features of the model is the absence of the Markov approximation. The resulting coupling constant is determined by thermal correlation functions of the quantized perturbation modes. Within this framework, we find that, for a representative set of parameter estimates, the characteristic decoherence timescale corresponding to the thermal contribution can be shorter than the Hubble timescale. In addition, we address the question of whether the pointer-state structure induced by the decoherence in such a framework could provide a criterion for the choice of semiclassical states in the early universe.</p>

                <h3>Probing Kerr spacetime via interferometric signatures of higher-order images</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Fabiano Feleppa, Fabio Aratore, Valerio Bozza, Lorenzo Albanese</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Higher-order images produced by photons that orbit close to the unstable photon region of a black hole encode information about the spacetime geometry and leave characteristic signatures accessible with long interferometric baselines. We develop an analytical description of these signatures for a compact source in the spacetime of a slowly rotating Kerr black hole. Using the strong deflection limit, we derive the complex visibility function for a source of finite size at linear order in the black-hole spin. For a static equatorial source, we obtain a direct relation between the dimensionless Kerr spin parameter and the angular displacement of successive higher-order images belonging to the same parity sequence. We then extend the construction to a compact source on a circular equatorial orbit by evaluating each image contribution at the corresponding retarded source position. Frame dragging and source motion modify the angular positions of the images and leave distinct imprints on the long-baseline visibility pattern. For the configuration considered here, these effects act in opposite angular directions, so that the resulting structure is determined by their competition. Our results provide an analytical framework for identifying the imprints of black-hole spin and source dynamics in the interferometric signatures of higher-order images.</p>

                <div>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Hairy black holes (BHs), characterized by nontrivial scalar or matter fields, introduce additional degrees of freedom beyond mass, charge, and spin, providing a framework for testing deviations from the Kerr paradigm. We investigate a class of rotating hairy black holes constructed within the gravitational decoupling framework, whose spacetime satisfies the Einstein field equations with a conserved energy-momentum tensor consistent with the strong energy conditions. In our previous work (Paper I; Dasgupta et al. 2026), we studied their horizon structure and test-particle dynamics and confronted two kinematic high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillation (HFQPO) models with observations of six black hole sources. Building on that analysis, we here test nine resonance models against the same HFQPO data, enabling a systematic comparison of eleven models (two kinematic and nine resonance) within the hairy Kerr framework. A comprehensive analysis based on the two kinematic models (Paper I) and the nine resonance models reveals that the HFQPO data with the current level of precision cannot rule out the hairy Kerr scenario. By implementing the Akaike Information Criterion and by examining the consistency of the inferred spins with previous independent spin estimates, our analysis provides a systematic framework for assessing the relative performance of different HFQPO models for each source. These results highlight the potential of HFQPOs to probe black hole hair and the need for more precise observations and a better understanding of the physical origin of QPOs.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Pre-geometric Gravity investigates the non-metric features of spacetime near the Planck scale, from which the gravitational interaction arises as a low-energy effective theory via a mechanism of spontaneous symmetry breaking. With a view of amending the classical singularities found in black hole geometries, in this work we study pre-geometric black hole configurations with spherical symmetry, and present exact solutions for different pre-geometric theories in vacuum via the correspondence principle. These solutions are the pre-geometric analogue of the (anti-)de Sitter-Schwarzschild metric, from which such type of black hole geometry is thus expected to emerge. In one case, the pre-geometric solution also exhibits an (anti-)de Sitter core of Planckian size. The main result is supplemented with an analysis of the pre-geometric version of Birkhoff's theorem.</p>

                <h3>Photon evolution through light-particle conversion in stochastic magnetic fields: Kramers--Kronig relations and universality</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Wataru Chiba, Ryusuke Jinno, Kimihiro Nomura</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-ph</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study photon conversion into light particles, such as dilatons, axions, and gravitons, induced by background magnetic fields, and formulate the resulting evolution in terms of the Stokes parameters. We show that photon conversion reduces to an effective non-unitary evolution of the photon sector. In the perturbative regime, the Hermitian and anti-Hermitian parts of the effective photon Hamiltonian are related through Kramers--Kronig relations, revealing that the changes in the Stokes parameters are not independent. We apply this general framework to photon evolution in Gaussian stochastic magnetic fields with possible helicity, and derive the ensemble-averaged evolution of the Stokes parameters. We find that two nonzero contributions arise even in the absence of magnetic helicity, which respectively correspond to the overall attenuation of all the Stokes parameters and to an irrelevant overall phase. We also find that magnetic helicity gives rise to two additional contributions, one of which changes the circular polarization while the other induces a rotation of linear polarization. These contributions form two Kramers--Kronig pairs. In particular, photon conversion induced by magnetic helicity is accompanied by both circular-polarization and birefringent responses. The same structure appears in dilaton-photon, axion-photon, and graviton-photon systems, revealing universality of photon conversion in magnetic fields.</p>

                <h3>Neutrino oscillations inside ultrarelativistic matter: on the role of the Tolman VI spacetime</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Daniele Gregoris</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-08</b></p>

                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>While both neutrino propagation in photons and ultrarelativistic plasmas and neutrino oscillations in curved spacetimes have been studied extensively, their combination in a self-gravitating geometry appears not to have been considered previously. In this paper, we will investigate neutrino oscillations inside a static spherically symmetric spacetime, derived self-consistently from Einstein's equations, supported by ultrarelativistic matter. By relying on the geodesic motion and geometrical symmetries of the configuration, we will compute analytically the neutrino eikonal and spinoptics phase oscillations. Next, we will relate resonance phenomena to the physical interpretation of the background material inside which neutrinos travel for disentangling gravitational versus electroweak effects. We will inspect the effects of the pure gravitational and pure matter fields, and of the temperature in the neutrino oscillations; we will explain why our results are not coordinate artifacts, and we will certify our heuristic method by comparing with the asymptotic behaviours predicted by thermal field theory approaches. We will raise awareness on the relevance of the spinoptics phase shift entering the flavor conversion probability, should the neutrinos hit a curvature singularity. Theoretically, we will scrutinize the separate roles of geometrical symmetries versus physical features of the configuration, while astrophysically we will qualitatively discuss neutrino oscillations inside stars and in the Cosmic Microwave Background at different temperature and density conditions. Our research puts forward, in the context of the Tolman VI metric, an observational method for identifying naked singularities in our Universe: neutrinos would simultaneously be physically overlapped, in flavor-equilibrium and quantum-mechanically scrambled.</p>
